newsitem.title: EGYPT: Australia, Egypt accord focuses on poppy detection.
newsitem.headline: Australia, Egypt accord focuses on poppy detection.

text.p: Australia signed an agreement on Monday to provide Egypt with special detection equipment that should speed up sales of Australian pulses, delayed in the past by quarantine procedures for stray poppy seeds.
The high-tech equipment can check bulk cargoes and distinguish between the seeds of harmless species of poppy and the seeds of opium poppies used in narcotics.

Australian Ambassador Mike Smith said: "It (the agreement) will help speed up the trade, not just the Australian trade, but for other countries that are involved in bringing pulses into Egypt because it will enable a very rapid identification of the sorts of poppy seeds that are located."
The machines, which operate on genetic engineering principles, will help reduce quarantine times, Mohammad Maguid, research officer at the Australian embassy, told Reuters.

Egypt's agriculture and justice ministries will receive the equipment under a memorandum of understanding signed by Australian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Trade Tim Fischer and Egyptian Deputy Prime Minister Youssef Wali.
Fischer was in Egypt as part of a Middle East tour to increase Australia's commercial ties.

"We in fact are providing some high-tech machinery which will detect poppy seeds and distinguish the naughty poppy seeds from the nice poppy seeds, the naughty ones being associated with the illicit drugs industry," Fischer told reporters.

"We bedded down two agreements formally, and informally we committed to encouraging further investment between Australia and Egypt, the sort of practical investment the Australian Wheat Board is making in the flour mill at Suez," he said.
Australia is a main source of wheat to Egypt but the accord aims mostly to increase their trade in pulses.
Poppy seeds grow freely among Australian fava bean fields and flecks the harvest or bulk shipments.
"It will help expedite the quarantine processes," said Maguid. "With this type of equipment they can know the genetic image of every type, there are about eight or nine types of poppy.
"Now these poppies are not narcotic. But according to Egyptian laws anything with the word poppy, it's forbidden."
He said that under the current arrangements, when quarantine authorities detect a poppy seed, they send it to the prosecutor's office. It is planted and grows in a month.

"So what happens now is the plant quarantine people will be able to diagnose properly the type of poppy and give the answer within hours," he said. "The Australian exporters and Egyptian importers were upset by the delay."
The two sides also signed an aviation accord to expand air links, said Fischer, who is also visiting Lebanon, Jordan, Israel, Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, and Gaza.
